meta.title: [2026 Guide] SIM Card & SMS Reception in Thailand | Nomad in Thailand
meta.desc: Complete guide to the best SIM strategy (AIS/True) and maintaining a Japanese phone number (SMS authentication). Covering Rakuten Mobile vs povo 2.0, dual SIM setup, and essential connectivity for nomads.

hero.title: [2026 Guide] Thailand SIM Strategy
hero.subtitle:
AIS, True, and Rakuten Mobile.
Build the strongest connectivity environment.

intro.p1:
"Which local SIM has the best signal?"
"I can't receive SMS authentication to log in to my Japanese accounts..."
intro.p2: These are common troubles digital nomad beginners face. The stress of no internet is immeasurable, and losing access to Japanese banking or credit card sites can threaten your livelihood.
intro.p3:
In conclusion, the strongest lineup in Thailand is "Dual SIM".
A local high-speed line and a SIM for maintaining your Japanese number. Managing these two on one smartphone is the smart standard for 2026.

sim.desc: The communication card you put in your phone. Recently, "eSIM" (no physical card) is mainstream. Super convenient as you just download it.

roaming.desc:
Using your home carrier's signal abroad.
Warning: Often extremely expensive (e.g., ~$20/day), so keep it off basically.

dual.desc: Putting two communication contracts in one phone (e.g., Local eSIM + Home Physical SIM).

roaming.desc: $20/day x 30 days. Outrageously expensive. Don't use except in emergencies.

wifi.desc: Bulky and requires charging. Also expensive. Outdated.

local.desc: Overwhelmingly cheap. Buy at airports or city shops. Speeds often faster than home.

dualSim.title: 2026 Correct Answer: "Strongest Dual SIM Setup"
dualSim.desc:
This is the optimal solution for living comfortably in Thailand.
Combine "Local High-Speed Data" and "Home Number Maintenance".

thaiSim.title: [1st SIM] Which Thai SIM is Best?

warning.title: [Warning] Airports are Expensive!
warning.desc:
Counters at the airport often sell expensive "Tourist SIM" packages (e.g., 299 THB for 8 days).
If you need internet from day one, get 1GB via Airalo beforehand, then contract a monthly plan (e.g., 200 THB for 30 days) at a city shop for the cheapest route.

thaiSim.desc: Thailand has two major carriers: "AIS" and "True". Neither is a bad choice, but here are the distinctions.

features.0: Widest coverage, connects easily even on islands/rural areas
Many plans include free access to city Wi-Fi spots (True Wi-Fi)

japanSim.title: [2nd SIM] How to Receive SMS?
japanSim.desc:
Even abroad, you'll be asked for "SMS Authentication" to log in to home sites (banks, credit cards, gov services). If you cancel your home number, you'll be stuck.
The following two services with free (or cheap) roaming are strongest for Japanese nomads.

rakuten.name: 1. Rakuten Mobile
rakuten.desc: Using "Rakuten Link App" makes calls to Japan free. This is a massive benefit. You can call clients or family with your number. It also comes with 2GB free roaming, serving as a lifeline upon landing.

povo.name: 2. povo 2.0 (au)
povo.desc: Hold a number for $0 base fee. However, you must top-up once every 180 days to avoid cancellation. For those who "just want to keep the number cheaply".

step1.title: Unlock SIM
step1.desc: Smartphones bought from carriers may be "SIM Locked". Be sure to unlock it via your account page before leaving. If not, local SIMs won't work.

step2.title: APN Settings (If needed)
step2.desc: If internet doesn't connect after inserting the SIM, "APN Settings" are needed. Enter settings found on the SIM package (most modern phones set this automatically).

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Q. Will my LINE data be lost if I swap SIMs?
faq.a1: No, it won't. LINE account and chat history are saved on the phone (app), so you can use it as is. However, you need to transfer if changing devices.
faq.q2: Q. Is a Thai phone number necessary?
faq.a2: Yes, essential. It's needed for Grab (taxi app), food delivery, and condo contracts. Choose a SIM with voice capability, not just data.
faq.a3: Yes, 5G coverage in central Bangkok is wider than many other cities and blazing fast. Often faster than cafe Wi-Fi.
